name: PISA
seoDesc: PISA: work out PISA from the vmax and the α angle. A free health calculator with the formula, units and a worked example.
summary: Supply the vmax, the α angle, the mitral valve area and the volume flow rate and the PISA calculator solves for PISA. Think of it as a shortcut for an informed starting point to take to a clinician, not a diagnosis. The unit chips sit next to the boxes, which is where most hand-calculation mistakes start.

sections.title: How does the PISA calculator work?
sections.html:
The PISA calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports PISA in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you type in the vmax, the α angle, the mitral valve area (MVA) and the volume flow rate (VFR).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the PISA calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

R=3 × the square root of (10) × the square root of (vmax × mitral valve area (MVA) ÷ (vr × α angle)) ÷ the square root of (PI)
R=(1 ÷ 2) × the square root of (2) × the square root of (volume flow rate (VFR) ÷ vr) ÷ the square root of (PI)
Effective regurgitant orifice (ERO, EROA)=100 × volume flow rate (VFR) ÷ vmax
Velocity time integral (VTI)=100 × regurgitant volume (RVol) ÷ effective regurgitant orifice (ERO, EROA)
PISA=2 × PI × (R ^ 2)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

Before doubting the arithmetic, check the inputs: a unit chip on the wrong setting, a drop-down left at its default, or a percentage typed as a whole number rather than a decimal will each shift the answer by a clean power of ten.

sections.title: How are units and precision handled?
sections.html:
Every quantity with units carries a chip beside its box. Switching the chip does not change what you know, only how it is written: values are converted to a common internal base, the arithmetic happens there, and the answer is converted back for display. Mixing metres with feet in one calculation is therefore safe.

  • Speed, opening in centimeters per second
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Speed, opening in centimeters per second
  • Angle, opening in degrees
  • Length, opening in centimeters
  • Area, opening in square centimeters
  • Volume, opening in milliliters

Results are rounded for display but computed at full precision, so chaining one result into the next does not accumulate error. Very large and very small numbers switch to scientific notation rather than printing a run of zeros.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The PISA calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Preparing for an appointment so you can describe your numbers clearly
  • Tracking a measurement over time and understanding what changed
  • Deciding whether a reading is worth a second look
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the vmax, the α angle and the mitral valve area — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Compare two scenarios by changing the input that actually differs between them, and keep the rest fixed, so the difference you see is the difference you meant to test.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.
  • If a result surprises you, look at the order of magnitude before the digits: a plausible number in the wrong unit looks more convincing than an implausible one, and is easier to miss.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the PISA calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns PISA, derived from the vmax, the α angle and the mitral valve area. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the PISA calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the vmax, the α angle, the mitral valve area and the volume flow rate, which is 5 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.

faq.q: Can I enter vmax in a different unit?
faq.a: Yes. Vmax opens in centimeters per second and the chip beside it offers 25 units. The number you typed keeps its magnitude and only its label changes; the calculation itself happens in a common base unit, so mixing systems in one form is safe.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: Is the PISA calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.

faq.q: Do I have to fill in every box?
faq.a: Fill in the ones you know. The result boxes are computed from them, so you never enter a value the formula can derive — press Calculate and every result updates together.
